title: From Concept to Practice: an Automated LLM-aided UVM Machine for RTL Verification
problem: UVM testbench development is time-consuming and requires deep hardware verification expertise. Manual testbench creation is error-prone and labor-intensive.
motivation: Automated testbench generation with LLMs can significantly reduce verification time and improve coverage, enabling faster RTL design cycles.
method: An AI system called UVM2 automatically generates testbenches—code that verifies whether a hardware design works correctly—by reading circuit specifications, replacing the manual process where experts hand-write verification code. It then measures test coverage (which parts of the design were actually tested) and uses this information in a feedback loop to improve the tests iteratively. This addresses the core problems of verification being time-consuming and error-prone. The method achieves a 38.82× reduction in setup time and 87.44% code coverage.
key_novelty: The key idea is combining automatic test generation with coverage feedback, so tests automatically improve based on what parts of the design actually get tested.
limitations: Coverage metrics and generalization to complex RTL designs with diverse verification requirements unclear from abstract.
